_rule: The named organs of the organism on the front door. Every id is a real public repository in the estate index. Every figure is copied from that build's own record or live page (the 'from' field says where) and nothing here is estimated. A link means one build really carries or gates the other's code.

organs.name: Kar
organs.gloss: The conductor. Kar picks the work, hands it to the organ that owns it, and may not call anything done until the gate agrees.

organs.name: The gate
organs.gloss: It breaks the code on purpose, hundreds of ways. If the tests do not notice a break, the build does not ship.

figures.k: broken copies of one grader that its tests caught. The one survivor is listed with its reason.

organs.name: The immune system
organs.gloss: The guard at the door. It checks a message's signature before reading a single word of it, and remembers every attack it has seen.

organs.name: The library
organs.gloss: Everything proven is kept here as a readable rule. A rule only gets in if it still works on examples it has never seen.

organs.name: The night loop
organs.gloss: While everyone sleeps it goes over the day's work, tests itself on a local model, and keeps only what passed.

organs.name: This site
organs.gloss: You are here. This page runs three of the organs for real, in your browser: the same files, pinned by hash.

organs.name: SLM Suite
organs.gloss: A small model reads the complaint, a verified library does the law, and a gate stops anything invented. It says when it does not know.

figures.k: right or rightly abstained, on 80 unseen complaints (69 of 80)
for a model 14 times its size asked to do it alone (1 of 80)

organs.name: LIGHT
organs.gloss: The language the organs speak to each other: a lossless codec that gets smaller the more two ends already share.

figures.k: smaller, on the call book with a shared seed. We aimed for 15× and missed by 0.17.

organs.name: Liveware
organs.gloss: A whole living system you can verify in your own browser in ten minutes, attack test included.

figures.k: breaches in 11,112 attempts: every attack class, 10,000 random inputs and a 1,000-strong swarm

organs.name: The spend wall
organs.gloss: A wall in front of an AI agent's paid calls. The most a call could cost is set aside before the call goes, so the budget cannot be overrun.

figures.k: overruns across 60 simulated days of at least double the demand; the stop latched on day 40 and nothing passed after
broken copies of the wall caught by its tests

organs.name: Tally
organs.gloss: Re-adds an AI agent's spending ledger from scratch and says whether the books are honest.

organs.name: The mint
organs.gloss: Bring one repetitive task and a few examples. Walk out owning a small model that does it, with a receipt anyone can re-run.

figures.k: for the minted model against its base's 4 of 16
for a model about 7 times bigger, which beat ours. Kept on the receipt.

organs.name: Kardlings
organs.gloss: A picture card that is a working mind you own. Every check a card passes says how strong it was and how old it is.

figures.k: deliberately broken copies caught across 29 modules, on GitHub's own machines

organs.name: PixelWhisperer
organs.gloss: Kar's art engine. It draws every card's face from the card's own facts, the same on every machine.

organs.name: CiteLock
organs.gloss: Checks whether a quote really appears in its source. Our first version once passed a fake: "he said yes" inside "she said yes". We found it by running it, and fixed it.

figures.k: requires whole words; the fault and the fix are both on its page

organs.name: Conform
organs.gloss: Checks an AI's structured output against its schema. Version 1 silently skipped rules it did not understand; version 2 refuses them out loud.

organs.name: GlyphGuard
organs.gloss: Finds invisible and look-alike characters hidden in text. Running every input class showed version 1 missed a block of mathematical letters; fixed.

organs.name: Stale Proof
organs.gloss: A green tick has a best-before date. This says how much to still trust one, and when it must be run again.

organs.name: Veil
organs.gloss: Redacts a document and proves that what you are shown really came from the original.

organs.name: BenfordGap
organs.gloss: Screens a column of amounts for made-up or limit-dodging figures.

organs.name: The proven shelf
organs.gloss: A shop shelf that only admits listings whose proof can be re-run by the buyer.

organs.name: The antibody exchange
organs.gloss: When one gate catches a new attack, every gate learns it, after re-checking it for itself.

organs.name: Fall Kit
organs.gloss: The shared foundation the tools stand on: identity, signing, the codec, the mesh.

organs.name: Memory
organs.gloss: Memory filed by what it says, not where it was saved, so the same thought is never stored twice.

organs.name: The AI-first company
organs.gloss: A company the AI runs and you can audit: every outward action waits behind a human key.

organs.name: A firm, running
organs.gloss: A made-up 100-person firm running live on the stack: 90 agent seats, 10 human seats at the doors that must stay human.

organs.name: The blueprint
organs.gloss: The seat-by-seat design of that firm, with the rented software it replaces worked out line by line.

organs.name: Sovereign Enterprise
organs.gloss: The full company build: floors, proposals, and undo from end to end.

organs.name: Structure beats scale
organs.gloss: A 58-byte rule against a 14-billion-parameter model on unseen real sessions.

figures.k: for the 58-byte rule, kept exactly as measured

organs.name: The geometric ladder
organs.gloss: Seven sealed tests of computing by settling instead of stepping.

figures.k: sealed claims held. The 11 that failed are kept on the page.

organs.name: The settling cell
organs.gloss: Rung one: a small network that reads handwritten digits by relaxing into the answer.

organs.name: The living seed
organs.gloss: A 496-byte signed genome that grows a checked model on each device from that device's own data.

organs.name: The spore
organs.gloss: Send 32 bytes; the working build grows at the other end.

organs.name: The seed laptop
organs.gloss: Plant one signed seed on a bare machine and a whole owned office grows from it, offline.

organs.name: CSV Forge
organs.gloss: Drop a spreadsheet in your browser and leave with a tested model of it. It refuses to pretend when there is no signal.

organs.name: FallJustice
organs.gloss: Drafts the letter before action for a UK consumer claim, from verified law.

organs.name: The vault
organs.gloss: Encrypted books for a small firm: the ledger, the bank feed and the tax return, on your own machine.

organs.name: FallGarden
organs.gloss: A second brain you own, and the first place the estate was drawn as a living thing.

organs.name: Build Broadcast
organs.gloss: Watch the estate build something real, explained so a 12-year-old can follow.

organs.name: Fall World
organs.gloss: The whole estate as one place you can walk around.
